title: Home of a Planet Hunter
caption: ESO's 3.6-meter telescope under the Milky Way, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: At La Silla Observatory, the home of ESO's 3.6-meter telescope stands beneath a starry sky crossed by the Milky Way. The telescope is one of the most effective instruments available for finding planets around other stars.

It started work in 1977 and, more than 40 years on, is still producing important results. Regular improvements, including a new secondary mirror, have kept it among the most productive telescopes on the planet. It is also still the biggest telescope at La Silla.

Much of its planet-hunting power comes from HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher. HARPS is a spectrograph, an instrument that splits starlight into its colors. It watches for tiny shifts in a star's light as an unseen planet tugs the star back and forth. ESO says its precision is unmatched and that it holds many records in exoplanet research.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla Observatory. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the stars and the Milky Way appear brighter here than they would to a visitor at the site.
